purpose: Exemplar of a metadata-derivable HARD filter (customer tier). The filter step must strictly include ALL enterprise-tier docs and NO growth/startup docs.

input.question: Which enterprise customers have Twilio integration blockers?

expected_orchestrator_behavior.step_1_filter: scope_of_exploration MUST include every doc whose metadata.customer.tier == 'enterprise'. Docs where tier != 'enterprise' MUST be excluded — this is a hard filter. Content filter ('Twilio integration blockers') is not derivable from metadata alone, so per rule 3, enterprise docs stay in-scope even if their topics_tagged doesn't mention 'integration'.
expected_orchestrator_behavior.step_2_rescope: Does this meeting surface a Twilio integration blocker for the customer?
expected_orchestrator_behavior.step_4_signals: Only enterprise docs are examined. Sub-agents emit signals only when their body positively describes a Twilio-specific blocker (not any integration, not any customer platform).

exemplar_signals.finding_summary: Beacon SaaS flagged a webhook signature mismatch between Voxly and their Twilio TaskRouter deployment that has blocked go-live for three weeks.
exemplar_signals.reference_text_shape: A verbatim quote naming Twilio TaskRouter and the specific webhook/signature symptom.

exemplar_response_text: Among enterprise customers, one active Twilio integration blocker surfaced: **Beacon SaaS** [s1] reported a webhook signature mismatch with their Twilio TaskRouter that has held up their go-live for three weeks.
anti_patterns_this_run_should_avoid: Including growth or startup-tier docs in scope (this is a hard-filter violation).
Excluding an enterprise doc whose topics_tagged doesn't include 'integration' — you can only infer that from body content, which the orchestrator hasn't seen.
Emitting a signal for a non-Twilio integration issue (Zendesk, Salesforce, etc.) — the rescoped question is Twilio-specific.
